title: Subnet Conductor: Terraform module for cross-AZ subnet orchestration and gateway failover
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Implement a reusable Terraform module (Subnet Conductor) that codifies subnet tagging, multi-AZ NAT/IGW selection, endpoint attachments, and automated route reconciliation with built-in upgrade and health-check hooks. Target: private deployments (VPC) where we must guarantee predictable egress, fast failover between gateways, and safe in-place upgrades without impacting SLOs. The module should be opinionated but configurable and provide clear observability hooks (metrics, synthetic probes, alerts).
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module exposes inputs for AZ subnet maps, preferred egress strategy (per-AZ NAT vs shared IGW), and endpoint policies
Automated route table reconciler ensures routes reflect attached gateways/endpoints within 2 minutes of change and emits metric 'subnet_conductor.route_reconcile_latency_ms'
Upgrade hooks use create_before_destroy patterns for gateway replacements and provide a canary mode that upgrades a single AZ before global rollout
Synthetic health probe (HTTP/TCP) per subnet validates egress path; failures trigger automated failover and open an incident (PagerDuty link)
Module published to internal terraform registry with README, examples, and integration tests (Terratest) referenced in PR
design_decisions: Use 'conductor' abstraction that owns subnet-to-egress mapping and route reconciliation instead of scattering route logic across teams
Prefer per-AZ NAT gateways by default for single-tenant/private deployments to reduce cross-AZ bandwidth and improve latency; allow opt-in shared IGW via variable
Route reconciliation implemented as a small lambda (or equivalent) invoked by resource life-cycle hooks; it will be idempotent and emit metrics for debugging
Healthchecks run from a lightweight probe deployed into each subnet using minimal compute; probe results stored in CloudWatch metrics and used for automatic failover decisions
Upgrades orchestrated with canary AZ first, then parallel upgrade of remaining AZs, with a forced rollback window configurable (default 15 minutes)
implementation_notes: Terraform module structure: modules/subnet-conductor/main.tf, variables.tf, outputs.tf, examples/
Expose variables: az_subnet_map (map), preferred_egress_type (enum: 'per_az_nat'|'shared_igw'), endpoint_config (list of maps), enable_canary_upgrade (bool)
Make heavy use of lifecycle meta-argument for gateway replacement: create_before_destroy where supported; provide safeguards for providers that don't support it
Add 'dry_run' flag to reconciliation lambda for testing changes before applying
Document IAM requirements for the module and provide least-privilege policy snippets in the README
rollout_plan: Stage: publish module to internal registry and tag v0.1.0
Canary: deploy into a single customer/test VPC with 2 AZs; run 72-hour soak and monitor metrics/dashboards
Scale: enable for 10 pilot customers and gather feedback
GA: promote to default private-deploy templates and announce in infra channels
test_plan: Unit: Terraform validate + fmt + check for drift with terragrunt wrapper
Integration: Terratest suite that brings up a 2-AZ VPC, deploys module with per-AZ NAT, simulates gateway replacement, and verifies no packet loss > 1%
Chaos: simulate zone outage and ensure failover completes within configured SLO
Regression: include tests for route reconciliation idempotency and upgrade canary behavior
rollback_plan: If a canary upgrade causes regressions, automatically revert to prior gateway attachment (module supports pinning previous gateway ids) and trigger an incident runbook. Manual rollback instructions included in README with terraform state steps.
